title: Membrane Arena: a browser game about three coupled membranes, reward schemes, a shield, an amplifier and a stabilizer (SYNTHETIC classical simulation)
description: SYNTHETIC educational game, zero dependencies, offline, English and French. The player steers three coupled Oja-rule membranes that learn a planted pattern in noise, chooses a reward scheme, a cooperation setting, a 2-of-3 shield, a capped amplifier and a gain-clamped stabilizer, and watches a (1+1) evolution step. Scores are compared with the measured width-32 results of the crystallization-contest repository, with the source file cited next to each number. Includes a daily seeded contest, a plain-text share card and challenge links in the URL hash, and a Lab view with instruments, multi-seed ensembles with confidence intervals against the repository baselines, paired A/B tests and a replay. A brain page sizes layers of membranes with the 2f + 1 rule and joins them with delayed links called microtubules (a metaphor only; nothing models real neurons, microtubules or a brain), and the Quorum Keeper logic game builds and breaks such fault-tolerant brains against an exhaustive adversary; its level targets are tuned to each level's own seed. Classical simulation only: the JavaScript port is statistically comparable to the Python original, not bit-identical. No accounts, no network calls.
